add.issue.name: The runner's browser never answers some of the suite's waits

edit.description.md:
Why the 139 real-browser tests skip on CI after #19, and what to do about it.

Evidence (all gh calls with -R T-Crypt/oh-my-pocket): push runs 38429736022, 38429841208, 38429902721, 38429961722, 38431886203, 38433132571. Different test each run, always the 22.19 leg, always a wait that never resolves: a page's title (expired at 10.6 s and again at 31.5 s when the budget was thirty seconds), 'held back', 'both, after the raise', and one layout read at 844x390 taken before the dock settled. 638 of 640 tests pass in those runs, so the runner is not merely slow: the event the test waits for does not arrive.

First thing to investigate: src/server/browser/page.ts learns a page's title only from Target.targetInfoChanged (line 439). Nothing asks Chromium for the target's current info when a page is attached (Target.attachToTarget in src/server/browser.ts:290, then page.init()), so an event that arrives in that window is lost for good and the title stays empty. A read of Target.getTargetInfo on attach, and on each navigation, would close that one and say whether the others are the same shape.

Then: re-enable the browser tests on the runner (the workflow's PI_POCKET_BROWSER line and its comment), and confirm two green push runs in a row before trusting it.

Context: the browser tests still run on a workstation (npm test, 640 pass, 0 skipped), and in any Pi Pocket session started with a browser.
